ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The figure below is a “schematic diagram of the position of the western Pacific subtropical high ridge line.” <image1> When the western Pacific subtropical high ridge line moves to the position shown in the figure, what are the weather characteristics of North China?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure is a schematic map of the East Asia—western Pacific region, marked with the 100°E, 120°E, 140°E, and 160°E meridians and the 10°N, 20°N, and 30°N parallels; in the figure, the “western Pacific subtropical high ridge line” is roughly near 20°N, and its position is relatively south. Then reason: according to the rule that the summer monsoon rain belt advances as the subtropical high ridge line moves northward, when the subtropical high ridge line is still at a relatively low latitude, the main rain belt is still staying in the Yangtze River Basin or the Jianghuai area and has not yet advanced to North China. North China is north of the active rain belt at this time, and the conditions for water vapor and precipitation are insufficient, so the weather appears dry with little rain.

method.method_draft: First describe the map and note that the subtropical high ridge is located at a relatively low latitude near 20°N over the western Pacific. Then apply the rule of summer monsoon rain-belt movement: a southern subtropical high ridge corresponds to the rain belt remaining around the Yangtze/Jianghuai region rather than reaching North China. Since North China is north of the active rain belt at this stage, conclude that its weather is dry with little rainfall.
